title: Wire editable public menus into the current Frequency header

source.ref: Explicit human choice: Make it editable while preserving the current Frequency design

detail: Current Frequency code defaults seed the existing menu editor. Untouched legacy materialized defaults retain the current design. Edited header rows flow through cached visitor-only server markup and the private validated-session viewer endpoint; own-profile roles and existing menu visibility predicates remove hidden/private/unsafe destinations before serialization. Current Frequency desktop panels, mobile disclosures, search, ghost upgrade dialogs and timing controls consume authorized rows. Public header arbitrary grid/column controls are explicitly unavailable because the current Frequency design is retained. Tests cover edited/new/hidden/role-gated links, request failure fallback, actual mobile Escape/focus, nested ghost dialog keyboard ownership, settings and rendered server links. No production seeding or menu writes performed. Source, actual React SSR/jsdom and mocked SDK/API evidence only; integrated compile/CI, real authenticated browser and deployment acceptance remain separate. Pre-repair actual header negative control fails edited-menu tests.

verify.note: Source wiring guard; run focused header projection, viewer route, actual SSR/client/admin menu tests for behavioral evidence.
